title: Microsoft Edge: opt-in for launching Edge when Windows starts on managed devices
summary: Held because the admin UI's Learn link gives general Edge policy configuration instructions but does not document the named startup setting. The route itself is supported by the two cited pages; link the control to its policy reference instead. The roadmap facts, policy behaviours and registry details are supported.

claims.where: front matter: products; Scope
claims.claim: The roadmap product is Microsoft Edge.
claims.quote: "products": ["Microsoft Edge"]

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: Microsoft plans an opt-in experience for users on managed devices to choose whether Edge launches automatically when Windows starts.
claims.quote: Microsoft Edge will introduce an opt-in experience that allows users on managed devices to choose whether Edge launches automatically when Windows starts.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Administrators can manage this behaviour through LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled with opt-in, opt-out and user-choice configurations.
claims.quote: Administrators can also manage this behavior through the LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled policy with opt-in, opt-out, and user-choice configurations.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Governance controls
claims.claim: Enabling the policy makes Edge launch visibly automatically when Windows starts.
claims.quote: If you enable this policy, Microsoft Edge will launch visibly automatically when Windows starts.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance controls
claims.claim: Disabling the policy means Edge never launches visibly automatically when Windows starts.
claims.quote: If you disable this policy, Microsoft Edge will never launch visibly automatically when Windows starts.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: When the policy is unconfigured, Edge does not launch automatically at Windows startup by default.
claims.quote: If you don't configure this policy, Microsoft Edge won't launch automatically when Windows starts by default.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationales
claims.claim: With the policy unconfigured, users are periodically shown an opt-in banner to turn automatic launch on.
claims.quote: Users are periodically shown an opt-in banner to turn it on, and can enable or disable automatic launch anytime from settings.

claims.claim: When the policy is unconfigured, users can enable or disable automatic launch at any time from settings.
claims.quote: Users are periodically shown an opt-in banner to turn it on, and can enable or disable automatic launch anytime from settings.

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The UI row's configure-microsoft-edge docs link documents the control's own final step, Launch Microsoft Edge on Windows startup.
claims.quote: Searched: LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled admin center. Opened https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/configure-microsoft-edge: gives the Microsoft Edge parent path, not the startup setting. Opened the cited LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled reference: it supplies the final label.
claims.fix: Change controls[0].ui.docs and the matching admin UI table link to https://learn.microsoft.com/deployedge/microsoft-edge-policies/launchedgeonwindowsstartupenabled. Keep the existing path and retain configure-microsoft-edge in sources: together the pages document the complete route.

claims.where: controls[0].ui.path; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The Group Policy Editor route is Computer Configuration > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge > Launch Microsoft Edge on Windows startup.
claims.quote:
open the Group Policy Editor and go to (Computer Configuration or User Configuration) > Policies > Administrative Templates > Microsoft Edge.
GP name: Launch Microsoft Edge on Windows startup
GP path (Mandatory): Administrative Templates/Microsoft Edge

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance

claims.quote:
Path (Mandatory): SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge
Value name: LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled
Value type: REG\_DWORD

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; controls[0].note; rationale: risk and impact
claims.claim: The default state is user-opt-in: without a configured policy, users choose whether to turn automatic launch on.
claims.quote: If you don't configure this policy, Microsoft Edge won't launch automatically when Windows starts by default. Users are periodically shown an opt-in banner to turn it on, and can enable or disable automatic launch anytime from settings.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The roadmap description and policy page describe a launch setting, not new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled autolaunch data access permissions admin center separate switch. Read the roadmap description and full policy reference; neither describes new data access.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: The documented control for this item is LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled, with no other feature-specific control identified.
claims.quote: Searched: LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled Microsoft Edge management service admin center opt-in banner frequency rollout; autolaunch data access permissions admin center separate switch. Opened the policy reference and Edge policy configuration page; found the same policy, not another control.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The policy page documents the opt-in banner and user settings, but no separate admin-centre switch for this item.
claims.quote: Searched: LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled autolaunch data access permissions admin center separate switch. Opened the full policy reference: it describes the banner and settings, and lists Group Policy and registry settings, not a separate admin-centre switch.

claims.where: Open questions
claims.claim: The policy page calls the banner periodic without stating a frequency.
claims.quote: Searched: "LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled" "banner" "frequency" "rollout". Opened the full policy reference and Stable release notes; the policy says "periodically" and gives no frequency.

claims.where: Why it matters; Scope; Open questions
claims.claim: The controlled-rollout documentation gives no fixed date for rollout to any particular tenant.
claims.quote: Searched: "LaunchEdgeOnWindowsStartupEnabled" "banner" "frequency" "rollout". Read the Stable release entries for 156 and 158 and the policy reference; they give no tenant-specific rollout date. The roadmap supplies only December CY2026 as a target.
